message.content:
The Declaration of Independence was signed by 56 delegates to the Continental Congress. Some of the most well‑known signers include:

| Signer | State | Notable Contributions |
|--------|-------|-----------------------|
| **John Hancock** | Massachusetts | President of the Second Continental Congress; his bold signature became a symbol of American patriotism. |
| **Thomas Jefferson** | Virginia | Principal author of the Declaration; later became the third U.S. President. |
| **Benjamin Franklin** | Pennsylvania | Renowned statesman, scientist, and diplomat; helped secure French support during the Revolution. |
| **George Washington** | Virginia | Commander-in-Chief of the Continental Army; later became the first U.S. President. |
| **James Madison** | Virginia | Known as the “Father of the Constitution”; later became the fourth U.S. President. |
| **Alexander Hamilton** | New York | Founding Father and first Secretary of the Treasury; key figure in establishing the federal financial system. |
| **John Adams** | Massachusetts | Diplomat in Europe; later became the second U.S. President. |
| **Samuel Adams** | Massachusetts | Revolutionary leader and political theorist; helped organize the Boston Tea Party. |
| **Patrick Henry** | Virginia | Famous for his “Give me liberty, or give me death!” speech; served as Governor of Virginia. |
| **John Jay** | New York | Diplomat and co-author of the Federalist Papers; later became the first Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. |

These individuals, along with 46 others, signed the Declaration on August 2, 1776, formally declaring the thirteen colonies independent from Great Britain.
